Bathroom Remodeling in Eastborough, KS

Eastborough is one of Wichita's most distinguished historic enclaves — a small incorporated community of primarily 1920s through 1950s custom homes set on tree-lined streets. These homes were built at a level of quality and detail that puts them in a different category from standard residential construction. The bathrooms reflect that heritage: original tile work in period-appropriate patterns, quality cast-iron fixtures, detailed millwork, and a character that no amount of remodeling trends can replicate.

Renovating an Eastborough bathroom is fundamentally different from renovating a bathroom in a 1990s Andover subdivision. The materials are better. The existing work is more detailed. The preservation question is real. And the expectation for what the finished result should look like — and what it should be worth — is higher.

Wheatland Construction remodels bathrooms in Eastborough and this corridor of established east Wichita. We're a Veterans Approved Builder (ID: 00899), Home Advisor Certified since 2019, and family-owned since 2018. We approach Eastborough bathrooms with the craft standard these homes deserve.

Eastborough Bathroom Remodeling Approach

Preservation first: Original period tile in good condition — 1930s hex mosaic, original subway tile, period-correct wall patterns — is evaluated before any demo decision. When the original tile is worth preserving, we preserve it. When it's past saving, we source period-appropriate replacements rather than defaulting to generic contractor tile.

High-end fixture specification: Eastborough homes call for quality fixtures — not builder-grade. Delta's standard line is not the answer for a 1938 custom home. We spec fixtures appropriate to the home's character: unlacquered brass, oil-rubbed bronze, porcelain-handle cross fixtures, freestanding soaking tubs where the layout supports it.

Cast-iron drain lines: Pre-1950 Eastborough homes are prime candidates for cast-iron drain assessment before tile-setting. Camera inspection before closing is the right call.

Galvanized supply: Homes of this era often still have original galvanized supply. We assess condition and provide transparent options.

What We Build in Eastborough Bathrooms

  • Period-sensitive tile restoration or replacement — hex mosaic, subway tile, period-correct patterns
  • Custom or semi-custom vanity cabinetry appropriate to the home's architectural character
  • Premium fixture specification — quality brands, period-appropriate finishes
  • Full plumbing infrastructure assessment with camera inspection of drains
  • Heated floor systems in primary baths where clients want them

Permits in Eastborough

City of Eastborough for all properties. We handle all permits.

How We Approach Bathroom Remodeling in

Every bathroom remodel in starts with an in-person assessment. We walk the existing bathroom with you, look at what's behind the walls where it matters (around the tub/shower surround, under the vanity, at the subfloor where it meets the tub), and give you an honest read on what the project actually involves before any numbers get discussed.

We price in writing. Every line item - demo, plumbing, tile, vanity, fixtures, exhaust, permit - is documented before work starts. No surprises mid-project.

Our crew handles demo through final walkthrough. We don't hand off your project to a rotating cast of subcontractors who don't know each other's work. The people who pull the permits are the people who do the work and stand behind it.

Wheatland Construction has held Veterans Approved Builder status (ID: 00899) since we opened and has been Home Advisor Certified since 2019. We're licensed and insured in Kansas. If something isn't right at the final walkthrough, we fix it before we consider the project done.

In Eastborough, the independent municipality status means separate permitting from Wichita. We work with Eastborough's permit process specifically. Custom homes here from the 1940s through 1990s require renovation work that matches the quality of the home's original construction.

Frequently Asked Questions About Bathroom Remodeling in Eastborough

How much does bathroom remodeling cost in Eastborough, KS?

Eastborough bathroom remodels range from $15,000 for a targeted period-sensitive refresh to $60,000+ for a full custom primary bath renovation with premium fixtures, custom cabinetry, heated floors, and plumbing infrastructure updates. The market and the homes here support the investment. Written, line-item estimates.

Can you match original period tile in an Eastborough bathroom?

For major repairs or partial tile replacement, often yes — we source from specialty suppliers who stock reproduction hex mosaic and period subway profiles. For full replacements where original tile is gone, we select contemporary equivalents that respect the home's era.

Do I need to demo all the original tile in my Eastborough bathroom?

Not necessarily. We assess the original tile — condition, substrate, grout — and give you an honest answer about whether preservation or replacement is the right call for each element. We don't default to full demo in these homes.

What fixtures do you recommend for a 1940s Eastborough bathroom?

Period-appropriate hardware and fixtures: unlacquered brass or oil-rubbed bronze finishes, cross-handle or cross-lever valves, undermount or vessel sinks appropriate to the style, freestanding soaking tub in the primary bath if the layout supports it. We discuss options at the consultation.

How long does an Eastborough bathroom remodel take?

3–6 weeks for most projects. Custom work, period-sourced tile procurement, and plumbing infrastructure work add time. We give you a realistic schedule at the consultation.

Does bathroom remodeling add value in Eastborough?

Yes, meaningfully. Eastborough properties trade at a premium and buyers here are sophisticated. A bathroom that respects the home's character and uses quality materials returns proportionally in appraised value — far more than a generic contractor remodel would.
